raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

This PR speeds up decode on Qwen3.5-architecture models by removing work from every gated delta net (GDN) layer and from Model Runner V2's per-step attention metadata. On Qwen3.8-27B at TP4 on B300, decode at batch 1 is **5.8% faster without speculation and 5.6% faster with MTP**. It is independent of #62800, #62962, #62963 and #62964.

At batch 1 a GDN decode step is a long chain of short kernels plus host-side metadata work, so each GEMM, copy or metadata build it drops shows up directly in per-token latency. With this PR each GDN layer runs one projection GEMM instead of two and reads its gates in place, the one-shot fused all-reduce and RMSNorm triggers PDL completion early on FlashInfer 0.7.2 and newer, and the full-attention KV cache groups of one spec share one metadata build.

## Claims

- `in_proj_ba` runs inside the `in_proj_qkvz` GEMM. Per GDN layer at one token (Qwen3.8-27B shapes at TP4 on B300, CUDA graph, cold L2), the two GEMMs take 9.98 us and 3.72 us, and the fused GEMM takes 10.05 us.
- Packed decode reads the `b` and `a` gates as strided views, which removes one copy kernel of about 1.3 us per GDN layer and step. This part comes from #51954 and is credited below.
- The spec-decode gated RMSNorm reads the output gate in place through a shared-weight mode of `layer_norm_fwd`. At 16 verify rows it takes 2.73 us per layer instead of 6.36 us, and its output is bitwise equal from 1 to 16384 rows.
- With FlashInfer 0.7.2 or newer, the one-shot fused all-reduce and RMSNorm triggers PDL completion early, which saves 1.9 us per all-reduce at TP2 and 1.4 us at TP4. #45448 moved the trigger to the end because of a stale read that FlashInfer 0.7.2 fixes, and older FlashInfer versions keep the end trigger.
- Model Runner V2 shares attention metadata across the full-attention KV cache groups of one spec, as it already does for Mamba groups (#58762) and as the V1 runner does. Qwen3.8-27B at TP4 has 6 full-attention groups, so each step makes 5 fewer metadata builds.

## Validation

AI assistance (Claude) was used to prepare this change; I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests listed below.

I served 33 SPEED-Bench prompts one at a time (greedy, 384 new tokens, thinking off) on Qwen3.8-27B at TP4 on 4x B300, with Model Runner V2 and prefix caching off, and started the servers in base, PR, PR, base order. Both builds ran on upstream `main` at `40210d8317`, the PR build with this PR's commits only. The per-kernel timings under Claims were measured on the earlier base `56e67b46a3`.

| Config | Base, decode tok/s at batch 1 | This PR | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| No speculation | 221.1 / 221.4 | 234.1 / 234.0 | +5.8% |
| MTP, 3 tokens | 503.8 / 504.7 | 533.2 / 532.2 | +5.6% |

Each cell is the median per request on one server, two servers per build, and higher is better. Mean MTP acceptance length stays close, 3.13 and 3.11 on the base servers against 3.06 and 3.08 with this PR. The MTP servers log no inference-time JIT warning, and each no-speculation server, base included, logs one for `_fused_post_conv_kernel`.

The fused GEMM rounds bf16 differently, so greedy outputs change, while the gate, norm and PDL changes are bitwise neutral. 9 of 33 prompts match base exactly, which is close to how often base at batch 1 matches base at batch 16 (7 of 33), and each build reproduces itself across restarts (33 of 33). On GSM8K (first 500 test questions, zero-shot chat, greedy, two servers per build), base scores 94.4% and 95.0% and this PR 94.6% and 95.4%.

For the PDL change, I called the fused op the way vLLM's pass does (bf16, 16 x 5120, one-shot, PDL on) and compared every output bitwise with the same step without PDL. FlashInfer 0.7.2 gives 0 stale reads in 50 steps at TP2 and in 200 at TP4, eager and in CUDA graphs. With FlashInfer's fix reverted, the same chain reads a stale residual in every step. This is a synthetic reproducer, separate from #45448's Kimi-K2.6 plus EAGLE-3 setup.

The new tests cover the fused projection, packed decode with strided gates at the kernel and the layer level, the shared-weight norm bitwise and at its call site, and metadata sharing together with the kernel-page refresh. On CPU on this base (`537a79f0fc`, `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`, one pytest process per file), the touched test files and the attention, KV-cache and worker files they depend on pass 857 tests, against 799 on `main`, with no new failures. The 15 failures are the same on both trees, 7 in `test_gpu_model_runner.py` and 8 CPU-builder cases in `test_group_head_counts.py`. `main` also failed `test_is_kv_cache_spec_uniform` in this run, on its 60 s subprocess-import timeout. On B300 the same files passed 628 tests with no failures on `40210d8317`, against 529 on `main` there. The 2-GPU all-reduce fusion test passed on the previous base, and `pre-commit` (mypy included) passes on this range.

```bash
pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD
python -m pytest -q tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_fused_in_proj.py tests/kernels/fla/test_fused_recurrent_packed_decode.py tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_packed_decode_strided_gates.py tests/kernels/fla/test_layer_norm_shared_weight.py tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B --tensor-parallel-size 4 --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-seqs 16 --no-enable-prefix-caching [--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}']
```

## Not a duplicate

I ran the duplicate-work searches from `AGENTS.md` §1 (open PRs, with keywords for `in_proj_ba`, GDN gate copies, the gated norm, PDL and `trigger_completion_at_end`, metadata reuse, GDN state indices and `flashinfer_cutedsl` GEMMs). Apart from #51954, this PR uses no code from the related PRs below.

- #51954 (packed decode reads the gates in place) is included as its own commit with its original author. If #51954 lands first, this commit drops out.
- #57318 routes the separate `in_proj_ba` GEMM to FlashInfer `mm_bf16` for small batches, as an opt-in. This PR folds that GEMM away on the unquantized, TP-sharded CUDA path, and #57318 still applies to the quantized, LoRA and Marlin-replicated paths that keep it. Both edit the same lines in `forward_cuda`.
- #41457 and optimization 3 of #55260 also remove the separate `ba` GEMM, through a 6-way `MergedColumnParallelLinear` with a new checkpoint mapping and through a fold for Qwen3-Next's interleaved layout. This PR folds after weight loading, so the loaders, the `in_proj_ba` module, LoRA and the quantized paths stay as they are.
- #58851 (cross-group reuse inside the GDN, Mamba and KDA builders) and #52297 (GDN batch-level spec metadata once per step) cover the per-group GDN and Mamba metadata cost. This PR extends #58762's reuse to full-attention groups, which neither covers. #58851 moves the same reuse code out of `update_block_table`, and #60426 (metadata reuse for AITER MLA and KDA on ROCm) lifts the same `MambaSpec`-only check in `attn_utils.py`, so whichever of these lands second rebases.
- #50279 fuses the GDN decode RMSNorm with a strided SiLU gate on SM103. This PR lets the spec-decode gated norm read the output gate in place, on every CUDA architecture. Both touch the gate tensor in `qwen_gdn_linear_attn.py`.
- #61577 lowers FlashInfer CuTeDSL BF16 GEMMs above 32 tokens to aten. This PR leaves GEMM routing as it is.

## Includes and credits

@feednetinfra wrote the packed-decode change that reads the `b` and `a` gates as strided views, and its kernel test, in #51954. Thank you. The commit keeps the original author and `Signed-off-by:`, is rebased onto current `main` (where the copy sits in the `qwen_gdn_attention_core` call), and adds a layer-level test.

## Details

- The fold appends the `ba` rows to `in_proj_qkvz`'s weight after loading, and both layers keep views of the fused tensor, so the weight loaders stay as they are. The fused rows are zero-padded to a multiple of 16, so the output's row stride stays divisible by 16 like an unfused output, and Triton kernels that read these views reuse the specialization compiled at warmup and graph capture.
- The shared-weight norm mode is a `SHARED_WEIGHT` constexpr in the JIT key, and the Qwen Triton warmup compiles the new keys.
- Metadata is shared only between groups with the same effective KV spec and builder type and no per-group inputs (`per_group_common_attn_kwargs` marks encoder-decoder cross attention). The reuse path refreshes the group's kernel-mapped block table before `update_block_table`, as a normal build does, so groups whose manager page is larger than the kernel page get kernel page ids. Without the refresh, 32 of the 64 kernel-page cases in `test_attn_utils.py` fail (16 on CPU, 16 on CUDA).
- #62962 (speculative-method registry) moves the same gate copy in `QwenGatedDeltaNetAttention._forward_core` for its own path. The two PRs merge without conflicts, and whichever lands second drops the resulting second pair of `b.contiguous()` and `a.contiguous()` calls.
- Size: +203 / -36 non-test lines and 495 test lines.

#64425 solve the same problem but a different way: use stream to paralyse the second gemm

It would be interesting is there difference

> https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64425 solve the same problem but a different way: use stream to paralyse the second gemm

The main reason I went with side-stream is that it doesn't require the two GEMMs to share the same quantization scheme, hence simpler code.

I'm closing this PR. The fold only beats the side stream from #64425 at one token per GDN step, where it speeds up decode at batch 1 without speculation by about 2%. At 4 to 16 tokens per step, which covers MTP verify at batch 1, the side stream already hides the `ba` GEMM. So the +1.3% with MTP in my last comment most likely comes from the fold's different bf16 rounding changing acceptance, not from a faster step, and a fold-only server gave 523.0 tok/s with MTP against 524.7 on main. A 2% gain in one config doesn't justify a second input-projection path and greedy outputs that no longer match main.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

I think you need to register a non-persistent buffer like https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f4edf9f0f078ae67392510aafd1871288948a3c3/vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/mamba_mixer2.py#L477

On reload (after previous record_metadata_for_reloading snapshotting), there will be a shape mismatch for in_proj_qkvz.weight. Concretely: in_proj_qkvz.weight would need to become a same-shape view into the new buffer too, the same way in_proj_ba.weight already is — right now in_proj_qkvz is the fused storage rather than a view of something else.

- The fold appends the `ba` rows to `in_proj_qkvz`'s weight after loading, and both layers keep views of the fused tensor, so the weight loaders stay as they are. The fused rows are zero-padded to a multiple of 16, so the output's row stride stays divisible by 16 like an unfused output, and Triton kernels that read these views reuse the specialization compiled at warmup and graph capture.
- The shared-weight norm mode is a `SHARED_WEIGHT` constexpr in the JIT key, and the Qwen Triton warmup compiles the new keys.
- Metadata is shared only between groups with the same effective KV spec and builder type and no per-group inputs (`per_group_common_attn_kwargs` marks encoder-decoder cross attention). The reuse path refreshes the group's kernel-mapped block table before `update_block_table`, as a normal build does, so groups whose manager page is larger than the kernel page get kernel page ids. Without the refresh, 32 of the 64 kernel-page cases in `test_attn_utils.py` fail (16 on CPU, 16 on CUDA).
- #62962 (speculative-method registry) moves the same gate copy in `QwenGatedDeltaNetAttention._forward_core` for its own path. The two PRs merge without conflicts, and whichever lands second drops the resulting second pair of `b.contiguous()` and `a.contiguous()` calls.
- Size: +203 / -36 non-test lines and 495 test lines.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""``QwenGatedDeltaNetAttention`` folds ``in_proj_ba`` into the qkvz GEMM.
+
+After loading, the qkvz and ba rows are stacked in one buffer so the CUDA
+forward runs one input GEMM per layer instead of two.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import types
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+from torch import nn
+
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.linear import UnquantizedLinearMethod
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.mamba.gdn import qwen_gdn_linear_attn
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.mamba.gdn.qwen_gdn_linear_attn import (
+    QwenGatedDeltaNetAttention,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.utils import default_unquantized_gemm
+from vllm.model_executor.model_loader.reload import (
+    finalize_layerwise_reload,
+    initialize_layerwise_reload,
+    record_metadata_for_reloading,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_utils import default_weight_loader
+
+HIDDEN = 64
+N_QKVZ = 96
+N_BA = 6  # 2 * num_v_heads / tp, not a multiple of 8
+
+
+class _Linear(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, n: int, k: int, quant_method=None) -> None:
+        super().__init__()
+        self.weight = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(n, k), requires_grad=False)
+        self.bias = None
+        self.quant_method = quant_method or UnquantizedLinearMethod()
+        self.calls = 0
+
+    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor):
+        self.calls += 1
+        return x @ self.weight.t(), None
+
+
+class _GDN(nn.Module):
+    """The input-projection part of ``QwenGatedDeltaNetAttention``."""
+
+    _can_fuse_in_proj = QwenGatedDeltaNetAttention._can_fuse_in_proj
+    process_weights_after_loading = (
+        QwenGatedDeltaNetAttention.process_weights_after_loading
+    )
+    project_input = QwenGatedDeltaNetAttention.project_input
+
+    def __init__(self, *, lora=False, disable_tp_ba=False, ba_quant_method=None):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.in_proj_qkvz = _Linear(N_QKVZ, HIDDEN)
+        self.in_proj_ba = _Linear(N_BA, HIDDEN, ba_quant_method)
+        self.in_proj_fused_split = None
+        self._ba_stream = None
+        self._lora_enabled = lora
+        self.disable_tp_for_ba_proj = disable_tp_ba
+        self.enable_fused_gdn_spec_decode = False
+        self._in_proj_fused_gemm = default_unquantized_gemm
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def on_cuda(monkeypatch):
+    platform = types.SimpleNamespace(is_cuda=lambda: True)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(qwen_gdn_linear_attn, "current_platform", platform)
+
+
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_fused_projection_matches_separate(default_vllm_config, on_cuda) -> None:
+    layer = _GDN()
+    x = torch.randn(5, HIDDEN)
+    ref_qkvz = x @ layer.in_proj_qkvz.weight.t()
+    ref_ba = x @ layer.in_proj_ba.weight.t()
+
+    layer.process_weights_after_loading(torch.float32)
+
+    assert layer.in_proj_fused_split == (N_QKVZ, N_BA)
+    fused = layer.in_proj_fused_weight
+    assert fused.shape == (112, HIDDEN)  # 96 + 6 rows padded to a multiple of 16
+    assert torch.count_nonzero(fused[N_QKVZ + N_BA :]) == 0
+    assert "in_proj_fused_weight" not in layer.state_dict()
+    # Both weights keep their shapes as views of their rows, so weight loading
+    # still lands there.
+    qkvz_w, ba_w = layer.in_proj_qkvz.weight, layer.in_proj_ba.weight
+    assert qkvz_w.shape == (N_QKVZ, HIDDEN)
+    assert qkvz_w.data_ptr() == fused.data_ptr()
+    assert ba_w.shape == (N_BA, HIDDEN)
+    assert ba_w.data_ptr() == fused.data_ptr() + N_QKVZ * HIDDEN * fused.element_size()
+
+    qkvz, ba = layer.project_input(x)
+    assert layer.in_proj_qkvz.calls == layer.in_proj_ba.calls == 0
+    torch.testing.assert_close(qkvz, ref_qkvz)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(ba, ref_ba)
+
+    # A later write through in_proj_ba (e.g. a weight reload) reaches the GEMM.
+    ba_w.data.zero_()
+    _, ba = layer.project_input(x)
+    assert torch.count_nonzero(ba) == 0
+
+    # Idempotent.
+    layer.process_weights_after_loading(torch.float32)
+    assert layer.in_proj_fused_weight is fused
+    assert layer.in_proj_qkvz.weight.shape == (N_QKVZ, HIDDEN)
+
+
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_fused_projection_survives_layerwise_reload(
+    default_vllm_config, on_cuda, monkeypatch
+) -> None:
+    # The unquantized method does no post-load processing on CUDA.
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        UnquantizedLinearMethod, "process_weights_after_loading", lambda *_: None
+    )
+    layer = _GDN()
+    model = nn.Sequential(layer)
+    record_metadata_for_reloading(model)  # at model construction, before fusion
+    layer.process_weights_after_loading(torch.float32)
+    storage = layer.in_proj_ba.weight.untyped_storage().data_ptr()
+
+    new_qkvz = torch.randn(N_QKVZ, HIDDEN)
+    new_ba = torch.randn(N_BA, HIDDEN)
+    initialize_layerwise_reload(model)
+    for proj, value in ((layer.in_proj_qkvz, new_qkvz), (layer.in_proj_ba, new_ba)):
+        loader = getattr(proj.weight, "weight_loader", default_weight_loader)
+        loader(proj.weight, value)
+    finalize_layerwise_reload(model, model_config=None)
+
+    # The reload wrote into the storage the forward (and its CUDA graphs) reads.
+    fused = layer.in_proj_fused_weight
+    assert "in_proj_fused_weight" in layer._non_persistent_buffers_set
+    assert fused.untyped_storage().data_ptr() == storage
+    assert layer.in_proj_qkvz.weight.data_ptr() == fused.data_ptr()
+    torch.testing.assert_close(fused[:N_QKVZ], new_qkvz)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(fused[N_QKVZ : N_QKVZ + N_BA], new_ba)
+    assert torch.count_nonzero(fused[N_QKVZ + N_BA :]) == 0
+    x = torch.randn(3, HIDDEN)
+    qkvz, ba = layer.project_input(x)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(qkvz, x @ new_qkvz.t())
+    torch.testing.assert_close(ba, x @ new_ba.t())
+
+
+class _OtherMethod(UnquantizedLinearMethod):
+    pass
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "kwargs",
+    [
+        dict(lora=True),
+        dict(disable_tp_ba=True),
+        dict(ba_quant_method="other"),
+    ],
+)
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_not_fused(default_vllm_config, on_cuda, kwargs) -> None:
+    if kwargs.get("ba_quant_method") == "other":
+        kwargs["ba_quant_method"] = _OtherMethod()
+    layer = _GDN(**kwargs)
+    layer.process_weights_after_loading(torch.float32)
+    assert layer.in_proj_fused_split is None
+    assert layer.in_proj_qkvz.weight.shape == (N_QKVZ, HIDDEN)
+    layer.project_input(torch.randn(2, HIDDEN))
+    assert layer.in_proj_qkvz.calls == layer.in_proj_ba.calls == 1
+
+
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_not_fused_off_cuda(default_vllm_config, monkeypatch) -> None:
+    platform = types.SimpleNamespace(is_cuda=lambda: False)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(qwen_gdn_linear_attn, "current_platform", platform)
+    layer = _GDN()
+    layer.process_weights_after_loading(torch.float32)
+    assert layer.in_proj_fused_split is None

+    def process_weights_after_loading(self, act_dtype: torch.dtype) -> None:
+        """Fold in_proj_ba into the in_proj_qkvz GEMM.
+
+        in_proj_ba has only 2 * num_v_heads / tp output features, so as its own
+        GEMM it costs a full launch (often with a split-K reduction) per layer
+        and token. Its rows are stacked under in_proj_qkvz's in one buffer,
+        zero-padded to a multiple of 16 rows, and the forward runs one GEMM on
+        that buffer and slices the qkvz and ba parts out of its output. The
+        padding keeps the fused output's row stride divisible by 16 like an
+        unfused qkvz output, so Triton kernels that read these views (the
+        spec-decode conv, for one) keep the stride specialization that warmup
+        and graph capture compiled. Both layers keep their weights, at their
+        checkpoint shapes, as views of the buffer, so the weight loaders (a
+        later reload included) keep writing to the right rows.
+        """
+        if self.in_proj_fused_split is not None or not self._can_fuse_in_proj():
+            return
+        qkvz_w = self.in_proj_qkvz.weight
+        ba_w = self.in_proj_ba.weight
+        n_qkvz, n_ba = qkvz_w.shape[0], ba_w.shape[0]

+        )
+        qkvz_w.data = fused[:n_qkvz]
+        ba_w.data = fused[n_qkvz : n_qkvz + n_ba]

+        # conv_weights): checkpoints and reloads still see only the weights.
+        self.register_buffer("in_proj_fused_weight", fused, persistent=False)
+        self.in_proj_fused_split = (n_qkvz, n_ba)
+

I think you need to register a non-persistent buffer like https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f4edf9f0f078ae67392510aafd1871288948a3c3/vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/mamba_mixer2.py#L477

On reload (after previous record_metadata_for_reloading snapshotting), there will be a shape mismatch for in_proj_qkvz.weight. Concretely: in_proj_qkvz.weight would need to become a same-shape view into the new buffer too, the same way in_proj_ba.weight already is — right now in_proj_qkvz is the fused storage rather than a view of something else.

The fused qkvz + ba rows now live in a non-persistent buffer on the GDN layer, the way Mamba2 does it, and in_proj_qkvz.weight and in_proj_ba.weight are both same-shape views into it, so a layerwise reload writes straight into the storage the forward and its CUDA graphs read. #64425 solve the same problem but a different way: use stream to paralyse the second gemm

It would be interesting is there difference

> https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64425 solve the same problem but a different way: use stream to paralyse the second gemm

The main reason I went with side-stream is that it doesn't require the two GEMMs to share the same quantization scheme, hence simpler code.

I'm closing this PR. The fold only beats the side stream from #64425 at one token per GDN step, where it speeds up decode at batch 1 without speculation by about 2%. At 4 to 16 tokens per step, which covers MTP verify at batch 1, the side stream already hides the `ba` GEMM. So the +1.3% with MTP in my last comment most likely comes from the fold's different bf16 rounding changing acceptance, not from a faster step, and a fold-only server gave 523.0 tok/s with MTP against 524.7 on main. A 2% gain in one config doesn't justify a second input-projection path and greedy outputs that no longer match main.
